rationale: The book's core identification that righteousness is the doing of God's commandments (the law kept and worn as righteous acts) is the most direct and economical explanation of the definitional texts it cites and of the garment symbolism developed across the full chapter. Deut 6:25, Ps 119:172 and 1 John 3:7 state the equation without remainder; Rev 19:8 (dikaiōmata) and the wedding-garment narrative confirm that the required covering consists of those acts. The strongest counter (forensic imputation as primary sense) must treat the same verses as secondary, obsolete, or merely evidential, introducing extra steps the book avoids. Secondary elaborations (gift-then-worn, washable, covenant clothing, armor) follow consistently from the same OT patterns and do not undermine the core. Residual tension with Pauline 'credited apart from works' language remains but is not fatal to the identification of the term itself on the supplied evidence.
book_core_identification: Righteousness is the doing of God's commandments—the law kept—worn as the garment of righteous acts.
book_secondary_elaborations: not a vague goodness nor a verdict only received
fine linen of Rev 19:8 is dikaiōmata (righteous deeds) given by God and put on by the saints
garment can be soiled by the doer's uncleanness and must be washed/kept
covenant covering (skirt/wing) that both clothes and binds to the commands
armor of God is God's own clothing (Isa 59:17) lent and worn as conduct
strongest_counter_interpretation: Righteousness primarily denotes a forensic/legal status of right standing before God that is imputed or credited to the believer through faith in Christ (apart from works), frequently pictured as a clean robe of Christ's own righteousness covering the sinner; ethical deeds are the subsequent fruit or evidence of that status rather than the essence of the term.
counter_core_identification: forensic/imputed right standing with God received by faith
material_core_denial: denies that the core referent of 'righteousness' is the active doing of the commandments rather than a received legal verdict or status
counter_case: Gen 15:6 / Rom 4:3-8: faith is credited as righteousness apart from works
Rom 3:21-26: righteousness of God manifested apart from the law through faith in Christ
Phil 3:9: not a righteousness of my own derived from the law but that which is through faith
2 Cor 5:21: exchange whereby we become the righteousness of God in him
Isa 64:6 commonly read as rendering all human righteousnesses worthless for standing
traditional Protestant reading of the wedding garment as Christ's imputed righteousness
book_explanatory_advantages: Matches the plain definitional statements of Deut 6:25, Ps 119:172 and 1 John 3:7 without remainder or reclassification as 'old-covenant only'
Accurately renders the Greek of Rev 19:8 as the righteous acts of the saints that constitute the fine linen
Explains why lack of the garment (i.e., lack of the acts) is the sole ground for expulsion from the wedding and why garments must be kept unspotted and washed
Coheres with the book's uniform method of establishing symbols from multiple independent OT witnesses
Gives a coherent non-dismissive reading of 'filthy rags' (stained by the unclean doer, not inherently filthy obedience) and of the washing texts
counter_explanatory_advantages: Integrates the major Pauline 'credited / apart from works / righteousness of God' passages more smoothly
Explains how sinners can possess perfect standing before God
Aligns with the dominant Reformation confessional tradition on justification
unresolved_objections: How the identification of righteousness as law-kept coheres with the Pauline language of righteousness credited by faith apart from works of the law (Rom 4; Phil 3:9)
Whether every occurrence of 'righteousness of God' is fully captured by the human doing of commandments
